mechanism: automation gated behind hours of manual play
claim: Autobuyers unlock only after many resets/hours of clicking; players asked for them sooner
player_reaction: "Please make automation unlock earlier, I don't want to get carpal tunnel because I need to spam clicks for many hours to unlock autobuyers"; another: "The game should be fully automated, MUCH SOONER, just like ... antimatter dimensions"; one player defended the late timing as deliberate

mechanism: teach by experimentation; show the core automation concept in the first level, not after 30-45 min of hand work
claim: Old tutorial took about 30-45 minutes to reach automation, constrained actions so players learned the tutorial not the concepts; new design lists "Showing and teaching core concepts like Assembling machines and electricity in the first level" and "Teaching by experimentation instead of jumping through arbitrary tasks"
player_reaction: Devs said the hand-mining opening made it look like a Minecraft clone

claim: FFF #342 'The new old tutorial': the team dropped the redesigned introduction because it did not match the game's vision; only the snippet was read, so the reason is not verified

source: https://www.softpedia.com (via search snippet, AdVenture Capitalist page)
mechanism: tedium-then-purchasable-automation: tap by hand at first, earn enough to hire managers who run the business
claim: Write-up says clicking every business gets too boring and the player hires managers to automate; managers do not remove decisions, the player still buys ventures and upgrades
player_reaction: Guides say to hire managers as early as possible

mechanism: manual click first, automation offered as soon as money exists; chained tiers (AutoClipper then MegaClipper at a count threshold)
claim: Starts with one button, other options open quickly, player sells clips to fund machines that build clips; MegaClippers appear after 75 AutoClippers (fan wiki). No designer statement on why.
Pecorella's Math of Idle Games part III (prestige) says nothing about teaching or unlocking automation; null for this question
GDC 2015/2016 Pecorella idle-game talks are partly paywalled; descriptions cover loops, retention, monetization, nothing on teaching automation

mechanism: Work tab priority grid, 1-4 per colonist per job
claim: Players report the Work tab is hard to read for newcomers (left-to-right order is the priority meaning) and the tutorial does not explain it; a common trick is set everything to 2, then set each colonist's first job to 1. Fluffy's Work Tab mod popular
player_reaction: Described as a tad confusing; some find 1-4 too few levels

claim: Players found the autobuy priority system confusing
player_reaction: One said it seems to glitch and not work properly

claim: A player could not find a guide for how automations work; reply said buy-type automations buy the lowest item available
player_reaction: Behaviour had to be explained by another player

mechanism: players built their own triggers (auto-sell, auto-equip, spend mastery tokens)
claim: Third-party userscripts for auto-sell, trigger actions and mastery spending exist, which signals unmet demand; I did not confirm what the base game offers

mechanism: community scripts (Kitten Scientists, Script Kitties) fill the automation gap
claim: Players run external scripts; one says default settings give good results for most stages; a 2014 poster found clicking catnip useful only in the earliest stage

mechanism: red dot above a tab when something new happens
claim: Dev added the dot because beginners would notice it; Just Another Idle v0.30 moved toasts into a panel opened by a button that shows a red dot
Genre splits into clickers (active input) and idle games (automation); blog pieces call the automation unlock one of the most exciting moments. SEO-grade support only

mechanism: autobuyers unlocked by achievements or challenges, upgraded by purchase
claim: Fan guides say autobuyers come from achievements and challenges (Big Crunch autobuyer needs Challenge 12 for its fastest interval). The wiki page returned HTTP 402, so no unlock sequence or design intent was read
player_reaction: Guide: turn them all on for quality of life
